Multiple organ failure secondary to complications of cosmetic surgery was the cause of death stated on the autopsy report of businesswoman Shiryl Anabe Saturnino, who died at The Icon Clinic in Mandaluyong City on Sunday.

Emil Sumangil reported on 24 Oras that these findings were presented during the case conference of Special Investigation Task Group Shiryl on Thursday.

If Saturnino's death is proven to be the result of their neglect, Dr. Samuel Eric Calderon Yapjuangco, anesthesiologist Dr. Jose Jovito Cordero Mendiola and nurses Virgil Alec Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove, and Audrey Michelle Santos will face criminal and administrative cases.

"Nakikita kong may negligence on part of The Icon Clinic, considering na yung initial requirements para mag-exist ang isang medical clinic ay hindi nila nasunod," SITG Shiryl Commander P/Sr. Supt. Marcelino Pedrozo said.

"We are contemplating to file reckless imprudence resulting to homicide," Pedrozo added. "That will lead to the reprimand, suspension, and revocation of the license of the doctors or the nurses involved."

The task force ruled to have Saturnino's histopathology examination prioritized at the PNP crime lab to allow them to charge medical personnel involved in her fatal surgery.

"At least nakausap na natin yung mga medical doctors natin. Although may resulta na sa autopsy ang recommendation nila, hintayin pa talaga yung hispathological examination dahil mas detalyado yun," Mandaluyong Police chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said.

Among other pieces of evidence police are considering in the case are the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) IDs presented by doctors and nurses.

Saturnino's medical records since her first medical procedure at The Icon Clinic in 2013 and a letter of consent signed by the victim were also presented during the case conference.

Dr. Briccio G. Alcantara, Philippine Association of Plastic Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons

A 29-year-old patient died after undergoing three aesthetic procedures at a clinic on Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong City, Cedric Castillo reported on 24 Oras.

Shiryl Saturnino was reported on Tuesday to have died at The Icon Clinic hours after she entered its operating room at 5 p.m. on Saturday for a liposuction, butt, and breast augmentation.

The Icon Clinic's staff noticed that Saturnino no longer had a pulse at 3 a.m. on Sunday after all her procedures have been completed.

Mandaluyong City Police Chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said the doctor who performed Saturnino's operation called for an ambulance from the Makati Medical Center and tried to revive her but failed.

"Triny nilang ma-revive 'to around 2:40 pero nag-expire siya mga 3:21," Alva said.

Operating doctors Dr. Jose Jovito Mendiola and Dr. Samuel Yapjuangco, circulating nurse Virgil Alec Ongleo, nurse assistant Alvin Carl Genove, and staff nurse Audrey Michelle have submitted their licenses and documents to the police.

Alva clarified that they have yet to identify a suspect behind Saturnino's death.

"Kinausap ng mga investigator ko yung mga doctor. Kaya lang nagpeprepare pa sila ng statement, nagpapa-assist sila sa lawyer nila," he explained. "Ang pinaka magiging matibay na batayan natin ay yung resulta ng autopsy."

Saturnino's parents had no idea that her emergency was connected to aesthetic procedures until they found her dead.

"(Nadatnan namin) sa operating room. Pagdating namin ayun, nakatakip na siya ng ano, kumot. Actually, hindi ko alam na ganun yung daratnan ko, akala ko buhay pa siya," Sherly, Saturnino's mother, said.

"Wala po kaming alam. Lahat po nun, ng procedure po niya, wala po kaming alam," she continued.

Dante Anabe, Saturnino's uncle, said the family came to the clinic on Tuesday afternoon to ask for a refund for her niece's procedures.

article.description: Congress should act swiftly on a bill that will ease the registration of births, marriages and deaths of Filipinos and penalize those who take advantage of the system's weaknesses.

Two hundred Chinese nationals with fake birth certificates and 3.7 million Filipinos without birth certificates, of whom 1.4 million are ages 14 and younger. It’s about time Congress acted swiftly on a pending bill that will ease the registration of births, marriages and deaths of Filipinos and penalize those who take advantage of the system’s weaknesses. article.title: Shiryl Saturnino died of multiple organ failure after 3 cosmetic procedures —autopsy report
article.description: Multiple organ failure secondary to complications of cosmetic surgery was the cause of death stated on the autopsy report of businesswoman Shiryl Anabe Saturnino, who died at The Icon Clinic in Mandaluyong City on Sunday.

text.preview:
Multiple organ failure secondary to complications of cosmetic surgery was the cause of death stated on the autopsy report of businesswoman Shiryl Anabe Saturnino, who died at The Icon Clinic in Mandaluyong City on Sunday.

Emil Sumangil reported on 24 Oras that these findings were presented during the case conference of Special Investigation Task Group Shiryl on Thursday.

If Saturnino's death is proven to be the result of their neglect, Dr. Samuel Eric Calderon Yapjuangco, anesthesiologist Dr. Jose Jovito Cordero Mendiola and nurses Virgil Alec Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove, and Audrey Michelle Santos will face criminal and administrative cases.

"Nakikita kong may negligence on part of The Icon Clinic, considering na yung initial requirements para mag-exist ang isang medical clinic ay hindi nila nasunod," SITG Shiryl Commander P/Sr. Supt. Marcelino Pedrozo said.

"We are contemplating to file reckless imprudence resulting to homicide," Pedrozo added. "That will lead to the reprimand, suspension, and revocation of the license of the doctors or the nurses involved."

The task force ruled to have Saturnino's histopathology examination prioritized at the PNP crime lab to allow them to charge medical personnel involved in her fatal surgery.

"At least nakausap na natin yung mga medical doctors natin. Although may resulta na sa autopsy ang recommendation nila, hintayin pa talaga yung hispathological examination dahil mas detalyado yun," Mandaluyong Police chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said.

Among other pieces of evidence police are considering in the case are the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) IDs presented by doctors and nurses.

Saturnino's medical records since her first medical procedure at The Icon Clinic in 2013 and a letter of consent signed by the victim were also presented during the case conference.

article.title: Beauty clinic charged for woman’s death
article.description: Two doctors and three nurses of a beauty clinic were charged with reckless imprudence resulting in homicide before the Mandaluyong City prosecutor’s office yesterday in connection with a businesswoman’s death while undergoing cosmetic surgery.
article.text: MANILA, Philippines - Two doctors and three nurses of a beauty clinic were charged with reckless imprudence resulting in homicide before the Mandaluyong City prosecutor’s office yesterday in connection with a businesswoman’s death while undergoing cosmetic surgery. Police said Samuel Eric Yapjuangco was the anesthesiologist while Jose Jovito Mendiola performed breast augmentation, liposuction and Brazilian buttock lift on Sheryl Saturnino, 29, on March 26. Nurses Virgil Alex Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove and Audrey Michelle Santos assisted during the operation. Chief Superintendent Romulo Sapitula, Eastern Police District director, said the EPD submitted as evidence Saturnino’s death certificate, pathology results and testimonies of several witnesses. In filing the case yesterday, investigators were accompanied by Saturnino’s mother and family lawyer Ruel Asubar. Normally, a witness doesn’t do that. Sasagutin lang tanong mo. Siya, binabalik niya at dinadagdagan pa niya,” he told DZMM. On Tuesday, House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro quizzed Matibag on the NBI's investigation into the alleged threats that Duterte made against Marcos Jr. and his relatives, including the possibility that she already had an arrangement with someone to do so. Matibag, like previous witnesses from the NBI, said the bureau took Duterte's statements seriously because of the potential threat to national security. output.title: Matibag to shed light on probe into VP Sara Duterte's 'kill' threat — spox
output.description: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is expected to shed light on the agency’s probe into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged death threat against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., when he testifies before the impeachment court on Tuesday, the prosecution panel said Sunday.

text.preview:
National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is expected to shed light on the agency’s probe into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged death threat against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., when he testifies before the impeachment court on Tuesday, the prosecution panel said Sunday.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday, Atty. Benjamin Tolosa said Matibag is expected to provide key details that the first two witnesses could not cover due to the limited scope of their work.

“Lagi niya hong sinasabi [na] ang makakasagot diyan ay ‘yung intelligence service na, so diyan ho papasok si NBI Director Melvin Matibag,” Tolosa said, referring to the testimony of NBI Cybercrime Division chief Jeremy Lotoc.

(He kept saying that the intelligence service would be able to answer that, so that is where NBI Director Melvin Matibag comes in.)

output.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. output.title: FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa did NOT surrender to NBI
output.description: Several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are claiming that Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is the subject of an International Criminal Court warrant, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. This is false.

text.preview: Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. No verified reports support claims that Dela Rosa surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said the lawmaker has yet to be apprehended, noting that a manhunt to locate dela Rosa is ongoing. Amid rumors of a supposed arrest, several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are capitalizing on posts claiming that Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The posts are untrue and designed to attract clicks for monetization. VERA Files traced the earliest copy of the claim to an Aug. 3 post by an FB page advocating for the 2028 presidential bid of Vice President Sara Duterte. It carried a photo set of the fugitive lawmaker interacting with men in uniform. “In fact, we are already investigating, kasi nung 2022 merong 11 proyekto diyan na somehow related doon sa mga pinangalanan na Top 15 contractors,” Matibag told reporters.

(In fact, we are already investigating because, in 2022, there were 11 projects there that were somehow linked to those named among the top 15 contractors.)

articles.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
articles.description: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said. The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa. Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war. Dela Rosa left the Senate with Sen. Robinhood Padilla early on May 14. text.preview:
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Monday said it started its investigation into flood control projects in Taguig City, even as the Department of Justice (DOJ) clarified Monday that it did not order the probe.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the bureau was already looking into 11 flood control projects implemented in 2022 that were allegedly linked to some of the country's top 15 contractors.

“In fact, we are already investigating, kasi nung 2022 merong 11 proyekto diyan na somehow related doon sa mga pinangalanan na Top 15 contractors,” Matibag told reporters.

(In fact, we are already investigating because, in 2022, there were 11 projects there that were somehow linked to those named among the top 15 contractors.)

“Baka sabihin ninyo timing na naman. Anyway, public na naman ‘yan dahil sinasabi ni Senator Lacson, so I think we should mention it,” he added.

(You might say this is about timing again. Anyway, this is already public knowledge because Senator Lacson mentioned it, so I think we should mention it.)

Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, however, stressed that the DOJ did not direct the NBI to conduct the investigation, saying the bureau was acting under its own mandate.

“We will respect the independence of the NBI relative to their mandate to pursue investigations. First thing, hindi ito pinag-utos ng DOJ. This is pursuant to the mandate of the NBI to pursue all this,” Vida said.

(We will respect the independence of the NBI in carrying out its mandate to pursue investigations. First, the DOJ did not order this. This is pursuant to the NBI's mandate to pursue these matters.)

Vida said that should the case reach the DOJ, the department would act based on the evidence presented.

“Kung sakaling makarating sa DOJ ‘yan, it will be based on what are the pieces of evidence presented. Rule of law pa rin tayo,” he said.

articles.description: The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said. Speaking at a forum in Quezon City over the weekend, Matibag said the investigation had yielded documents and testimonies that could support criminal charges. “Within the next few days, perhaps within a week, we will be filing cases,” Matibag said. The investigation is part of the NBI’s broader probe into the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), which Matibag said involves multiple cases and a large volume of documents and testimonies. “We divided this into pieces so we can file cases. Matibag said the NBI had obtained documents concerning the cauldron, which reportedly cost P55 million, although the actual cost was allegedly only about P5 million. He said several leaders of sports associations were also being investigated, with some already appearing before the NBI after receiving subpoenas. Matibag said the NBI was also examining the activities of people associated with Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano, who was the head of PHISGOC in 2019. articles.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
articles.description: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said. The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa. Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war. Dela Rosa left the Senate with Sen. Robinhood Padilla early on May 14. articles.title: NBI chief Matibag did NOT step down
articles.description: A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post. Not true.

text.preview: Melvin Matibag stepped down from his post as director of the National Bureau of Investigation. As of May 21, Melvin Matibag continues to serve as NBI director. Reports that NBI agents who attempted to serve an ICC arrest warrant for Sen. Bato Dela Rosa “betrayed” him are false. A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post following the May 11 mayhem at the Senate involving an attempt to arrest Sen. Bato Dela Rosa. Not true. The NBI chief did not step down. The false claim originated from a YouTube channel that published a video on May 12 with a thumbnail that bore the text: “ MATIBAG BUMITAW NA. SENADO TINAPOS SI MATIBAG SA NBI? 9-NBI AGENT NILAGLAG SI MATIBAG (MATIBAG HAD STEPPED DOWN. SENATE ENDED MATIBAG AT NBI? 9 NBI AGENTS BETRAYED MATIBAG)” It surfaced the day after Dela Rosa appeared at the Senate for the first time since November 2025, when news came out that the International Criminal Court had issued a warrant for his arrest in connection with the crimes against humanity case in which the senator is named as a co-conspirator. NBI agents attempted to serve the arrest warrant, which prompted Dela Rosa to run, leading to a chase on a staircase from the parking area to the session hall, where the senator eventually obtained protective custody from Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano. Matibag continues to hold his position at the NBI. On May 21, he went to Legazpi City to lead the inauguration of the NBI Academy in the Bicol Region. The nine NBI personnel involved in chasing Dela Rosa were cited in contempt at the Senate and have since been turned over to the NBI as the bureau conducts its own investigation into the matter. There have been no reports from authorities or from the media that they “betrayed” Matibag in any way. articles.title: FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa did NOT surrender to NBI
articles.description: Several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are claiming that Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is the subject of an International Criminal Court warrant, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. This is false.

text.preview: Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. No verified reports support claims that Dela Rosa surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said the lawmaker has yet to be apprehended, noting that a manhunt to locate dela Rosa is ongoing. Amid rumors of a supposed arrest, several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are capitalizing on posts claiming that Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The posts are untrue and designed to attract clicks for monetization. VERA Files traced the earliest copy of the claim to an Aug. 3 post by an FB page advocating for the 2028 presidential bid of Vice President Sara Duterte. It carried a photo set of the fugitive lawmaker interacting with men in uniform. The post also bore the caption, “Senator bato delarosà sumukó na [shocked emoji] Sa mga NBÎ at nag salita at humingi… (Senator Bato dela Rosa has surrendered to the NBI, spoke out, and pleaded…),” but ended with the phrase “see more,” creating the impression that additional details would follow. A tactic employed by some disinformation peddlers previously flagged by VERA Files, the teaser seemed intended to entice users to click the photo set, which contained an embedded link that redirects them to a product page on a popular e-commerce platform. No verified reports substantiate online claims that dela Rosa surrendered to the NBI. In fact, the agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said that the senator wanted by the ICC has yet to be apprehended, adding that their manhunt operation to locate dela Rosa is still ongoing. text.preview: Defense counsel Mark Vinluan cross-examines National Bureau of Investigation Melvin Matibag on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team on Wednesday will continue the cross-examination of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on the ninth day of her impeachment trial. Constitutional law expert Domingo Egon Cayosa cautioned the defense about how to cross-examine a “competent witness” like Matibag. “Binabalik niya yung tanong at dinadagdagan pa niya,” Cayosa reasoned. “Meron pa siyang counter-attack. Normally, a witness doesn’t do that. Sasagutin lang tanong mo. Siya, binabalik niya at dinadagdagan pa niya,” he told DZMM. On Tuesday, House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro quizzed Matibag on the NBI's investigation into the alleged threats that Duterte made against Marcos Jr. and his relatives, including the possibility that she already had an arrangement with someone to do so. Matibag, like previous witnesses from the NBI, said the bureau took Duterte's statements seriously because of the potential threat to national security. He added that the NBI already had persons of interest — people who may be involved in an investigation but who are not suspects — but said he could not disclose who they are. Defense counsel Mark Vinluan stressed his team's objection to the Lascañas affidavit, which was submitted to the International Criminal Court but that Matibag had no personal knowledge on. articles.description: The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment tri

text.preview: NBI Director Melvin Matibag takes the witness stand on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment trial and continues on Wednesday. Matibag is the prosecution’s final witness for the fourth article, which accuses Duterte of committing grave threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and his relatives and inciting to sedition through said alleged threats. Impeachment Trial of Sara Duterte His appearance came months after he was appointed as NBI chief. Before joining the Marcos administration, however, Matibag was considered an ally of the vice president’s father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, having held several key posts during the previous administration. A TEACHERS’ SON Matibag’s parents began their careers as teachers before later joining government service. His father taught at Claro M. Recto High School, while his mother served as a teacher at Pedro Pelaez Elementary School. He is married to Laguna First District Rep. Ma. Rene Ann Matibag. A lawyer by profession, Matibag earned his undergraduate degree in Philosophy from the University of Santo Tomas before obtaining his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University in 1996. He was admitted to the Philippine bar the following year and later completed a master’s degree in corporate and finance law at Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan. TIES TO THE DUTERTES Former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo appointed Matibag as general manager of the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) in 2010. article.title: NBI chief Matibag did NOT step down
article.description: A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post. Not true.

text.preview: Melvin Matibag stepped down from his post as director of the National Bureau of Investigation. As of May 21, Melvin Matibag continues to serve as NBI director. Reports that NBI agents who attempted to serve an ICC arrest warrant for Sen. Bato Dela Rosa “betrayed” him are false. A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post following the May 11 mayhem at the Senate involving an attempt to arrest Sen. Bato Dela Rosa. Not true. The NBI chief did not step down. The false claim originated from a YouTube channel that published a video on May 12 with a thumbnail that bore the text: “ MATIBAG BUMITAW NA. SENADO TINAPOS SI MATIBAG SA NBI? 9-NBI AGENT NILAGLAG SI MATIBAG (MATIBAG HAD STEPPED DOWN. SENATE ENDED MATIBAG AT NBI? 9 NBI AGENTS BETRAYED MATIBAG)” It surfaced the day after Dela Rosa appeared at the Senate for the first time since November 2025, when news came out that the International Criminal Court had issued a warrant for his arrest in connection with the crimes against humanity case in which the senator is named as a co-conspirator. NBI agents attempted to serve the arrest warrant, which prompted Dela Rosa to run, leading to a chase on a staircase from the parking area to the session hall, where the senator eventually obtained protective custody from Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano. Matibag continues to hold his position at the NBI. On May 21, he went to Legazpi City to lead the inauguration of the NBI Academy in the Bicol Region. The nine NBI personnel involved in chasing Dela Rosa were cited in contempt at the Senate and have since been turned over to the NBI as the bureau conducts its own investigation into the matter. There have been no reports from authorities or from the media that they “betrayed” Matibag in any way. article.description: Several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are claiming that Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is the subject of an International Criminal Court warrant, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. This is false.

Amid rumors of a supposed arrest, several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are capitalizing on posts claiming that Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The posts are untrue and designed to attract clicks for monetization. VERA Files traced the earliest copy of the claim to an Aug. 3 post by an FB page advocating for the 2028 presidential bid of Vice President Sara Duterte. It carried a photo set of the fugitive lawmaker interacting with men in uniform. A tactic employed by some disinformation peddlers previously flagged by VERA Files, the teaser seemed intended to entice users to click the photo set, which contained an embedded link that redirects them to a product page on a popular e-commerce platform. article.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
article.description: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said. The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa. Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war. article.title: NBI chief Matibag did NOT step down
article.description: A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post. Not true.

text.preview: Melvin Matibag stepped down from his post as director of the National Bureau of Investigation. As of May 21, Melvin Matibag continues to serve as NBI director. Reports that NBI agents who attempted to serve an ICC arrest warrant for Sen. Bato Dela Rosa “betrayed” him are false. A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post following the May 11 mayhem at the Senate involving an attempt to arrest Sen. Bato Dela Rosa. Not true. The NBI chief did not step down. The false claim originated from a YouTube channel that published a video on May 12 with a thumbnail that bore the text: “ MATIBAG BUMITAW NA. SENADO TINAPOS SI MATIBAG SA NBI? 9-NBI AGENT NILAGLAG SI MATIBAG (MATIBAG HAD STEPPED DOWN. NBI agents attempted to serve the arrest warrant, which prompted Dela Rosa to run, leading to a chase on a staircase from the parking area to the session hall, where the senator eventually obtained protective custody from Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano. Matibag continues to hold his position at the NBI. On May 21, he went to Legazpi City to lead the inauguration of the NBI Academy in the Bicol Region. article.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
article.description: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.

text.preview: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said. The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa. Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war. Dela Rosa left the Senate with Sen. Robinhood Padilla early on May 14. output.text: A tragic incident involving a family from the Philippines in Baldwin Park, California, has left three family members dead, including two children, in what police describe as a brutal stabbing attack. Authorities have arrested a 23-year-old male suspect, who is believed to be related to the victims. The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner identified the victims as 8-year-old Mia Chantelle Narvaez, 16-year-old Paul Sebastian Manangan, and 44-year-old Rona Nate. All three victims sustained fatal stab wounds to the upper body. Filipino siblings, 2 others shot dead in Southern California home According to a press release by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Baldwin Park police responded to a disturbance call on the 4700 block of Bogart Avenue on the evening of December 26. The suspect attempted to flee in a vehicle but crashed into a cul-de-sac before being detained. He was later booked for murder. Out of respect for the victims’ families, authorities have not disclosed the exact nature of the relationship between the suspect and the victims. However, investigators confirmed that the suspect lived at the residence. POLICE SEEK MORE INFORMATION ON INCIDENT According to local news reports , neighbors recounted chilling details of the incident, including the screams of a young girl running for help. “You heard the little girl screaming, coming out and crying for help, saying, ‘Someone call 911. My brother stabbed my mom in the back, I saw blood,’” shared Nathan Garcia to ABC7 news. Another neighbor, Edna Figueroa, expressed shock and fear over the incident, describing it as “a very scary feeling… to find out that this is happening in our neighborhood.” The family is believed to have Filipino roots, with neighbors confirming their shared heritage. The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Homicide Bureau is assisting Baldwin Park police with the ongoing investigation. The case will be presented to the Los Angeles County District Attorney’s Office for review and potential filing of charges. Authorities urge anyone with information about the incident to contact the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department Homicide Bureau at (323) 890-5500. Anonymous tips can also be submitted through “Crime Stoppers” at (800) 222-TIPS (8477) or via the P3 Tips mobile app. Meanwhile, a GoFundMe page has been created to "help the family grieve properly and say their goodbyes to their loved ones." output.title: 29-year-old patient dies after three procedures at cosmetic clinic
output.description: A 29-year-old patient died after undergoing three aesthetic procedures at a clinic on Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong City, Cedric Castillo reported on 24 Oras.
output.text:
A 29-year-old patient died after undergoing three aesthetic procedures at a clinic on Shaw Boulevard, Mandaluyong City, Cedric Castillo reported on 24 Oras.

Shiryl Saturnino was reported on Tuesday to have died at The Icon Clinic hours after she entered its operating room at 5 p.m. on Saturday for a liposuction, butt, and breast augmentation.

The Icon Clinic's staff noticed that Saturnino no longer had a pulse at 3 a.m. on Sunday after all her procedures have been completed.

Mandaluyong City Police Chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said the doctor who performed Saturnino's operation called for an ambulance from the Makati Medical Center and tried to revive her but failed.

"Triny nilang ma-revive 'to around 2:40 pero nag-expire siya mga 3:21," Alva said.

Operating doctors Dr. Jose Jovito Mendiola and Dr. Samuel Yapjuangco, circulating nurse Virgil Alec Ongleo, nurse assistant Alvin Carl Genove, and staff nurse Audrey Michelle have submitted their licenses and documents to the police.

Alva clarified that they have yet to identify a suspect behind Saturnino's death.

"Kinausap ng mga investigator ko yung mga doctor. Kaya lang nagpeprepare pa sila ng statement, nagpapa-assist sila sa lawyer nila," he explained. "Ang pinaka magiging matibay na batayan natin ay yung resulta ng autopsy."

Saturnino's parents had no idea that her emergency was connected to aesthetic procedures until they found her dead.

"(Nadatnan namin) sa operating room. Pagdating namin ayun, nakatakip na siya ng ano, kumot. Actually, hindi ko alam na ganun yung daratnan ko, akala ko buhay pa siya," Sherly, Saturnino's mother, said.

"Wala po kaming alam. Lahat po nun, ng procedure po niya, wala po kaming alam," she continued.

Dante Anabe, Saturnino's uncle, said the family came to the clinic on Tuesday afternoon to ask for a refund for her niece's procedures.

"Inalam namin kung how much did she pay, so nalaman namin kung magkano then we requested for a refund. And then granted naman yung refund," Anabe said.

Saturnino's family may press charges against The Icon Clinic.

"We're contemplating on that, we're just waiting for the result of the histopathology exam," Anabe said.

The Icon Clinic's legal counsel, Atty. Estelita D. Cordero, stressed that it was working with the police and Saturnino's family in addition to requesting five working days to submit affidavits pertinent to the case.

She added that Saturnino had been a regular patient for years and was cherished by the clinic.

"Ginagawa po namin ang lahat at kasalukuyan po kaming nakikipagtulungan sa abot ng aming makakaya upang malaman kung ano ang totoong nangyayari sa 'di inaasahang pagpanaw ni Bb. Saturnino," Cordero wrote.

She added, "Si Bb. Saturnino ay ilang taong nang regular pasyente ng The Icon Clinic at labis naming ikinalulungkot ang kanyang sinapit." —Rie Takumi/NB, GMA News

output.title: Shiryl Saturnino died of multiple organ failure after 3 cosmetic procedures —autopsy report
output.description: Multiple organ failure secondary to complications of cosmetic surgery was the cause of death stated on the autopsy report of businesswoman Shiryl Anabe Saturnino, who died at The Icon Clinic in Mandaluyong City on Sunday.
output.text:
Multiple organ failure secondary to complications of cosmetic surgery was the cause of death stated on the autopsy report of businesswoman Shiryl Anabe Saturnino, who died at The Icon Clinic in Mandaluyong City on Sunday.

Emil Sumangil reported on 24 Oras that these findings were presented during the case conference of Special Investigation Task Group Shiryl on Thursday.

If Saturnino's death is proven to be the result of their neglect, Dr. Samuel Eric Calderon Yapjuangco, anesthesiologist Dr. Jose Jovito Cordero Mendiola and nurses Virgil Alec Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove, and Audrey Michelle Santos will face criminal and administrative cases.

"Nakikita kong may negligence on part of The Icon Clinic, considering na yung initial requirements para mag-exist ang isang medical clinic ay hindi nila nasunod," SITG Shiryl Commander P/Sr. Supt. Marcelino Pedrozo said.

"We are contemplating to file reckless imprudence resulting to homicide," Pedrozo added. "That will lead to the reprimand, suspension, and revocation of the license of the doctors or the nurses involved."

The task force ruled to have Saturnino's histopathology examination prioritized at the PNP crime lab to allow them to charge medical personnel involved in her fatal surgery.

"At least nakausap na natin yung mga medical doctors natin. Although may resulta na sa autopsy ang recommendation nila, hintayin pa talaga yung hispathological examination dahil mas detalyado yun," Mandaluyong Police chief Sr. Supt. Joaquin Alva said.

Among other pieces of evidence police are considering in the case are the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC) IDs presented by doctors and nurses.

Saturnino's medical records since her first medical procedure at The Icon Clinic in 2013 and a letter of consent signed by the victim were also presented during the case conference.

Dr. Briccio G. Alcantara, Philippine Association of Plastic Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons Vice-President for Internal Affairs, said their group will also investigate Saturnino's death.

"Even a minor surgery under local, even in a medium surgery, there will always be a complication. And that complication is usually minimized by having exams na fit ang patient. Miniminimize but it may still happen," Alcantara said.

Neither Japjuangco nor Cordero have given a statement on the police's latest findings. —Rie Takumi/JST, GMA News

output.title: Beauty clinic charged for woman’s death
output.description: Two doctors and three nurses of a beauty clinic were charged with reckless imprudence resulting in homicide before the Mandaluyong City prosecutor’s office yesterday in connection with a businesswoman’s death while undergoing cosmetic surgery.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines - Two doctors and three nurses of a beauty clinic were charged with reckless imprudence resulting in homicide before the Mandaluyong City prosecutor’s office yesterday in connection with a businesswoman’s death while undergoing cosmetic surgery. Police said Samuel Eric Yapjuangco was the anesthesiologist while Jose Jovito Mendiola performed breast augmentation, liposuction and Brazilian buttock lift on Sheryl Saturnino, 29, on March 26. Nurses Virgil Alex Ongleo, Alvin Carl Genove and Audrey Michelle Santos assisted during the operation. Chief Superintendent Romulo Sapitula, Eastern Police District director, said the EPD submitted as evidence Saturnino’s death certificate, pathology results and testimonies of several witnesses. In filing the case yesterday, investigators were accompanied by Saturnino’s mother and family lawyer Ruel Asubar. output.text: MANILA, Philippines — Iniimbestigahan ng National Bureau of Investigation-Homicide Division ang pagkamatay ng isang ginang na sumailalim sa liposuction, tummy tuck, Brazilian butt lift, at bodytite for arms ng isang celebrity plastic surgeon, sa San Juan City noong Marso, 2, 2026. Casteel ay nagbayad ng P570,000 para sa nasabing procedures na umabot ng pitong oras, na-discharge matapos ang 3 araw na recovery period. Subalit pagkalipas ng apat na araw ay isinugod siya sa ospital at na-diagnosed ng “high-risk pulmonary embolisim” o isang medical emergency dahil sa blood clot na humarang sa daloy ng dugo sa baga at mapanganib na hindi normal na presyon ng dugo. output.text: EVERY Undas or All Souls Day (Nov. 2) when Filipinos troop to cemeteries to remember departed loved ones, I always think of the families of desaparecidos. Where do they go to offer flowers and light the candles for their dead whom they didn’t bury? I think of Edith Burgos, whose son Jonas was last seen on April 28, 2007 at the Ever Gotesco Mall. I think of University of the Philippines students Sherlyn Cadapan and Karen Empeno who were last seen on June 26, 2006 in Hagonoy, Bulacan. There are many more: Father Rudy Romano, a Redemptorist priest who served landless peasants and displaced settlers and the six workers of Paper Industries Corporation of the Philippines namely Joseph Belar, Jovencio Lagare, Romualdo Orcullo, Diosdado Oliver, Artemio Ayala Jr. and Arnold Dangkiasan. The list is long according to Asian Federation against Involuntary Disappearances (AFAD) and Families of Victims of Involuntary Disappearance (FIND) “For the families whose loved ones were made to disappear by their own governments, remembering the disappeared is a painful and torturous ordeal. They have no graves to visit, no tombs to light candles and no place to offer flowers. Even silence is an elusive desire to pray as the cry of their disappeared loved ones for truth and justice occupies their memories,” said Darwin Mendiola, AFAD project coordinator. This All Souls Day, I think of the 3,000 or more who were recently killed in President Duterte’s war against drugs. Last Saturday, the family of 34-year old Florjohn Cruz laid him to rest 10 days after he was killed in a round-up of suspected “pushers” in Caloocan City last Oct. 19. A cardboard with words, “Pusher at Adik, Huwag Tularan” was found near his dead body. Like many others who were killed the last three months since Duterte took power, the family said Cruz, a singer-musician, a hockey player and a dean’s lister in a computer school, had been hooked in drugs but he never engaged in drug pushing, He didn’t have a gun which belied police allegation that he was killed because he shot the arresting policemen. It’s double tragedy for the Rosales family who are still mourning the killing of their son Petronio Rosales Jr last October 26 while waiting for a ride in front of a restaurant along Yakal Street in Barangay San Antonio, Makati. Jhay-R, as Petronio is known to relatives and friends, has been living in the United Kingdom and came home when his sister Lauren was killed while riding in a jeepney last July. The killing was reported as related to the government’s campaign against illegal drugs. The family vehemently protests saying Lauren, an executive assistant in a food company, was never into illegal drugs. The culprits were never known nor arrested. Jhay-R, an IT expert, was reportedly following up Lauren’s Social Security Service benefits before he goes back to UK when he was killed last week. A retired policeman, Alfredo Jebulan, is very angry. His son, Yani, a student at Our Lady of Fatima University in Caloocan was shot to death by riding- in- tandem men wearing bonnets at around 12 midnight Oct. 29 2016. He said his son was not into drugs. He wrote a letter to President Duterte raging: “My point is, if I will know that one of your policemen has the hand for the cause of the death of my son, God forbids, I will let heaven and earth befall upon him. I know you don’t tolerate this but let me be very very frank, if they know how to kill people, so am I. This goes to you too Gen. Dela Rosa Sir. I’m begging you Help me solve the unnecessary death of my son PLEASE or I will be the one to do it without your help.” Jebulan’s letter is being shared in social media. But that is all. The killings continue. Enjoying “very good” satisfaction rating for his first 100 days performance dominated by killings unprecedented in the country’s history, Duterte vowed to kill more. “I tell you, I will triple it. ‘Pag hindi nasunod ang gusto ko, to get rid of my country (of the drug problem), you can expect 20,000 or 30,000 more (deaths),” Duterte said last week. News reports of killings, either by police officers or by vigilantes, have become a daily norm. People are no longer shocked. Poet Marne Kilates wrote in Facebook : “SAD. REALLY sad to see friends and acquaintances of apparently considerable intellectual capacity slip into the Pied Piper’s parade of lightweight flute music, or more frighteningly, into the discombobulated rationalizations for what really is the rantings of a deranged leader canonized by electoral process and the subsequent adulation and fawning of mass insanity.” “They forget, “ Marne rued, “in the process, the most basic features of a civilized community and a working democracy: the Rule of Law, Due Process, and Human Rights, Human Rights, Human Rights. They bristle and scamper away at the mere mention of these civilized concepts, like the aswangs of folklore when shown a crucifix. They are afraid of these concepts because they don’t know how to deal with them. Or these remind them that they are in fact in the wrong and would not admit it. They have regressed into the state of the not-so-noble savage pre-Enlightenment and pre-Renaissance, rushed across time and plunged into the all-gaming, all-dominating, and all-deceiving neo-fascist Gehenna of the Dark Internet.” We have lost our sense of outrage. We should be in a state of mourning. Receive fresh perspectives and explainers in your inbox every Tuesday and Friday. output.title: Enough of 'Alice Guos'!
output.description: Congress should act swiftly on a bill that will ease the registration of births, marriages and deaths of Filipinos and penalize those who take advantage of the system's weaknesses.
output.text: Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. Tita C. Valderama is an editor and trustee of VERA Files. She has been a journalist for more than 30 years. The numbers are appalling! Two hundred Chinese nationals with fake birth certificates and 3.7 million Filipinos without birth certificates, of whom 1.4 million are ages 14 and younger. It’s about time Congress acted swiftly on a pending bill that will ease the registration of births, marriages and deaths of Filipinos and penalize those who take advantage of the system’s weaknesses. The last comprehensive national law on civil registration, Republic Act 3753, or the Civil Registration Law, was enacted more than 90 years ago, in November 1930. The Philippine Legislators’ Committee on Population and Development Foundation (PLCPD) presented to the media last July 12 the salient features of the pending legislation, which has become relevant in view of the revelations in the Senate probe on the alleged involvement of suspended Bamban, Tarlac Mayor Alice Leal Guo in unlawful activities connected with the operations of the Philippine offshore gaming operation (POGO) hub in her town. From the Senate probe, it appears that Guo had a late registration of birth in November 2005, when she was 19 years old. As a consequence, the senators discovered several other irregularities in the process that made it apparently easy for the Bamban mayor to obtain Filipino citizenship. Sen. Sherwin Gatchalian said on Friday that foreigners managed to acquire Filipino citizenship practically overnight simply by paying P300,000 in exchange for a fraudulent birth certificate and driving license. He said this was the modus operandi uncovered by the National Bureau of Investigation involving 200 Chinese nationals who were able to secure certificates of live birth in 2018 and 2019 alone from the civil registry of Santa Cruz, Davao del Sur province. Because of this, Gatchalian is seeking a suspension of the policy that allows late registration of birth. But the PLCPD, a group of forward-looking lawmakers and advocates working on policies related to population and human development, noted that late registration is mostly in remote and disadvantaged areas where the process of acquiring a birth certificate is hindered by distance, low literacy or financial constraints. “Without a birth certificate, a child or an individual faces the risk of being denied [the] rights to identity, education, health services, inheritance, employment, and even legal justice in cases where determining the age is crucial,” Romeo Dongeto, executive director of PLCPD, explained. A birth certificate is usually required for school enrolment or when applying for a job, licenses, passport and other identification documents. “A birth certificate is every Filipino child’s passport to their hopes and dreams. We need to pass the Civil Registration bill to make birth registration free and accessible, especially for the most vulnerable Filipinos,” Dongeto said. The measure also involves modernizing and digitizing the civil registration system, as well as establishing barangay-level registration to reach more marginalized sectors. Registration of marriages and deaths is as important as legal documentation of births. Data from the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) show that many deaths go unreported due to logistical hurdles and cultural practices, particularly in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM), where only 42% of deaths were registered in 2021. Dennis Mapa, national statistician and civil registrar general, said an omnibus bill on civil registration and vital statistics is “long overdue and should be a legislative priority” to improve further the efficiency of the delivery of civil registration services as well as ensure the integrity of civil registry documents in the civil registry offices. “A death certificate is needed for surviving family members to access inheritance, social pensions, insurance and burial assistance. With an improved and accessible civil registration system, the government can properly assist these individuals and ensure that their rights are being upheld,” said lawyer Sophia Monica San Luis, a civil registry global expert. Sen. Risa Hontiveros, principal author of the Civil Registration bill in the Senate, said the falsification of civil registry documents, which is what the Guo family apparently did, must be stopped. “Our current investigation has revealed deep cracks in our systems that need correcting. It also exposed the ways our institutions have been corrupted by unscrupulous individuals who want to exploit the weaknesses of our people. The most vulnerable in society are affected by the lack of an efficient and honest civil registration and vital statistics system,” said Hontiveros, who is leading the probe into Guo’s alleged involvement in the POGOs’ illegal operations. “Delayed registration of birth happens,” she acknowledged, noting that this is a significant concern, especially among Filipinos who lack the financial means to obtain a birth certificate. However, she said: “It’s a different story if the weaknesses of our system are being abused, like in the case of the Guo family. A streamlined and strengthened civil registration and vital statistics system is needed to safeguard the safety, nationality and citizenship of the most vulnerable Filipinos.” To Tingog party-list Rep. Jude Acidre, a deputy majority leader at the House and one of the bill’s authors, emphasized that the benefits of an improved civil registration system do not end with the individual’s ability to access their rights; they also translate into foundational data that supports national progress. “If every birth or vital event of a Filipino is registered, we can generate accurate data. With accurate data, we can make evidence-based policies and decisions to ensure that no one is being left behind,” he pointed out. Health Department Undersecretary Emmie Liza Perez-Chiong, for her part, said reforming the civil registration system will address the huge gaps in the availability and quality of critical data on vital events of a person, including birth, marriage and death. Having accurate data is crucial in national health policy and planning and coordinating services for the Filipino population at all levels of the country’s health care system. output.title: PROFILE: Who is Melvin Matibag, the prosecution’s final witness on alleged threats? | ABS-CBN News
output.description: The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment tri
output.text: NBI Director Melvin Matibag takes the witness stand on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte at the Senate of the Philippines in Pasay City on Tuesday, July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — The testimony of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag was at the center of Vice President Sara Duterte’s eighth day of impeachment trial and continues on Wednesday. Matibag is the prosecution’s final witness for the fourth article, which accuses Duterte of committing grave threats against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. and his relatives and inciting to sedition through said alleged threats. Impeachment Trial of Sara Duterte His appearance came months after he was appointed as NBI chief. Before joining the Marcos administration, however, Matibag was considered an ally of the vice president’s father, former President Rodrigo Duterte, having held several key posts during the previous administration. A TEACHERS’ SON Matibag’s parents began their careers as teachers before later joining government service. His father taught at Claro M. Recto High School, while his mother served as a teacher at Pedro Pelaez Elementary School. He is married to Laguna First District Rep. Ma. Rene Ann Matibag. A lawyer by profession, Matibag earned his undergraduate degree in Philosophy from the University of Santo Tomas before obtaining his law degree from the Ateneo de Manila University in 1996. He was admitted to the Philippine bar the following year and later completed a master’s degree in corporate and finance law at Wayne State University in Detroit, Michigan. TIES TO THE DUTERTES Former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo appointed Matibag as general manager of the Manila International Airport Authority (MIAA) in 2010. In 2014, he served as convenor of Movement for Reform, Continuity and Momentum (More2Come), a group that advocated to amend the 1987 Constitution to allow then-President Benigno “Noynoy” Aquino III to seek another term. In 2017, the older Duterte appointed Matibag as president of the National Transmission Corporation (TransCo). Matibag later became acting secretary-general of Duterte’s political party, Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban), during a leadership dispute that split the party into two. In 2022, Duterte appointed him as acting cabinet secretary, a position that was later abolished by the Marcos administration. Matibag resigned as PDP-Laban acting secretary-general in 2023, saying his personal principles were no longer aligned with the party's direction. He also said he wanted to avoid any appearance of a conflict of interest because his wife belonged to a different political party. TIMELINE: The cracks in ruling party PDP-Laban before BBM endorsement OPINION PIECES AGAINST DUTERTE After leaving PDP-Laban, Matibag returned to private law practice and entered the academe, becoming the first dean of the Lyceum of Alabang College of Law. He also became a columnist for the Daily Tribune, where he wrote about the vice president. In October 2023, Matibag wrote in his column that he opposed the allocation of confidential and intelligence funds to the Office of the Vice President. He argued that the Constitution does not assign the vice president functions that would require such funds. At the time, he emphasized that his position was directed at the policy rather than Vice President Duterte personally. But nearly a year later, Matibag criticized Duterte in a September 2024 column and described her as a “bratinella” or a spoiled brat. In November of the same year, following Duterte’s controversial livestream that formed part of the impeachment case against her, Matibag published another opinion column. Matibag criticized Duterte’s remarks in the livestream and described her actions as “an ambitious power grab” that resulted in her “humiliating defeat.” He also again referred to her as a “bratinella.” At the impeachment trial, Matibag explained that it was the older Duterte who first used the moniker for her daughter, the vice president. SHIFT TO THE MARCOS ADMINISTRATION In September 2024, Matibag filed a disbarment complaint against former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque, a staunch ally of the Dutertes and his colleague during the Duterte administration. Matibag said the complaint included issues related to Roque's social media posts, including the so-called “polvoron” video involving Marcos. In August 2025, Matibag sought to return to government service by applying for the vacant position of Ombudsman but was not selected for the post. Instead, Marcos appointed him NBI director on February 19, 2026. This is also in the same period that a second round of impeachment complaints against Duterte were filed at the House of Representatives. Following his appointment, some questioned whether his selection was linked to his complaint against Roque. Matibag denied the allegation, saying his appointment was “not a reward.” Marcos to name ex-PDP exec Melvin Matibag as new NBI chief New NBI chief says appointment 'not a reward'
