output.title: Impeach trial Day 9: Matibag cross-examination to continue | ABS-CBN News
output.description: Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team on Wednesday will continue the cross-examination of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on
output.text: Defense counsel Mark Vinluan cross-examines National Bureau of Investigation Melvin Matibag on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — Vice President Sara Duterte’s defense team on Wednesday will continue the cross-examination of National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag on the ninth day of her impeachment trial. Constitutional law expert Domingo Egon Cayosa cautioned the defense about how to cross-examine a “competent witness” like Matibag. “Binabalik niya yung tanong at dinadagdagan pa niya,” Cayosa reasoned. “Meron pa siyang counter-attack. Normally, a witness doesn’t do that. Sasagutin lang tanong mo. Siya, binabalik niya at dinadagdagan pa niya,” he told DZMM. On Tuesday, House lead prosecutor Gerville Luistro quizzed Matibag on the NBI's investigation into the alleged threats that Duterte made against Marcos Jr. and his relatives, including the possibility that she already had an arrangement with someone to do so. Matibag, like previous witnesses from the NBI, said the bureau took Duterte's statements seriously because of the potential threat to national security. He added that the NBI already had persons of interest — people who may be involved in an investigation but who are not suspects — but said he could not disclose who they are. LASCAÑAS AFFIDAVIT The prosecution on Tuesday also showed a 2011 video of Duterte punching a court sheriff when she was still Davao City mayor and featured an excerpt of alleged Davao Death Squad hitman Arturo Lascañas' affidavit on drug-related killings to repeated objections from defense counsel Mark Vinluan. Defense counsel Mark Vinluan stressed his team's objection to the Lascañas affidavit, which was submitted to the International Criminal Court but that Matibag had no personal knowledge on. "We cannot allow this witness to build his testimony based on this document," Vinluan also said, pointing out the affidavit is unsigned and was not notarized. Luistro said the video and the affidavit were material since the NBI considered these in its investigation. Matibag also referred to the affidavit as "open source intelligence" that the NBI used for leads. Trial presiding officer Sen. Francis Escudero allowed the presentation of the affidavit but reminded senators that its contents were not necessarily true and that the impeachment court was not saying that they were. MATIBAG WIFE During cross-examination, Vinluan raised that Matibag is married to Laguna First District Rep. Ann Matibag, one of the House members who supported Duterte's impeachment. The NBI director said his wife's job "is totally detached" from his official duties. House prosecution panel spokesman Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong said Wednesday Rep. Matibag's work should not be used to cast doubt on the NBI investigation. “Obviously, the congresswoman has a different role from the work of the NBI chief,” Adiong told ANC's "Headstart". Adiong also defended Matibag’s writing of several anti-Duterte opinion columns prior to his stint as NBI chief, noting that the investigation was already ongoing before his appointment. Asked if the columns showed that Matibag had long been biased against Duterte, he said, “He shared his opinion but that did not negate the fact that the Vice President did utter those words…Whether or not Matibag has several leanings is not the subject matter of the investigation.” The NBI director is the last prosecution witness on Duterte's alleged threats. DEFENSE ‘HAPPY’ WITH INITIAL CROSS Meanwhile, Duterte’s defense team believes that “at least for this first half of the cross-examination, we were able to again meet our targets,” said panel spokesperson Atty. Michael Poa. “So, masaya naman kami sa nangyari. But definitely, hindi pa tayo tapos. So, itutuloy pa natin…and we'll see how things go,” Poa told reporters. Poa said they were testing the credibility of the NBI chief but added it was up to the impeachment court to say whether Matibag was a credible witness or not. “Well, that's really for the court to appreciate. Pero siyempre, ang point namin talaga is to test the credibility, Test kung may bias man o wala,” he said. TRUST RATING Poa also explained Vinluan’s line of questioning and the relevance of survey results showing the trust ratings of Duterte to the allegations of betrayal of public trust. “Pinakita lang naman natin na kung betrayal of public trust ang pinag-uusapan ng tao, yung tiwala ng tao sa ating Bise Presidente, pinakita lang natin at tinanong lang natin. Ang point lang naman nun is tinanong lang natin kung yung mga ganong bagay ay kino-consider din ng NBI sa kanilang investigation lalo na parating nababanggit yung katagang betrayal of public trust kanina,” Poa said. Poa added that the Lacañas documents were not an affidavit but a private document. “Kung it's a private document, then you have to prove that it was in fact duly executed or may due execution. Pag notaryado kasi, nagiging public document na siya. Whereas pag walang notaryo, private document lang siya. That's why sa amin, hindi namin siya tinatawag na affidavit kasi magiging affidavit lang naman ‘pag sumumpa ka sa katotohanan ng mga sinasabi mo, that goes for everyone. And dito sa instances na ito, hindi kasi nangyari yun,” he said. Poa also explained the team’s strategy to put an “x” mark on the documents presented during the trial and said this was not meant to mislead the public. “There was no intention to mislead the public. Ang point lang namin dun is gusto lang natin pakita through graphics kung ano yung may personal knowledge siya, ano yung wala. Para lang mas madaling ma-appreciate na itong dokumento na ito, wala kang personal knowledge. Itong pangalawang dokumento, wala rin siyang personal knowledge. It's really to show aling dokumento yung may personal knowledge sa wala,” he said. ‘HINDI NATIBAG’ Meanwhile, the House prosecution so far sees “no reason” to conduct a redirect examination on Matibag, according to one of its counsels, Atty. Benjamin Tolosa Jr. “So far, doon sa mga naging tanong kahapon, parang wala kaming nakikitang masyadong rason para kailangan pang mag-redirect, lalu na’t… hindi natibag ang naging statement ni NBI director kahapon,” Tolosa said. The prosecution also does not see a need to take back its previous manifestation to drop some witnesses for the impeachment article accusing Duterte of making grave threats. “When we said we can already waive the presentation of some of the witnesses... based ‘yan sa aming assessment na hindi na sila kailangan, dahil ‘yung kanilang intended testimony ay na-cover na ng mga naging testimonya ng aming mga naunang witnesses,” he said. — With a report from Jonathan De Santos, ABS-CBN News Defense counsel Mark Vinluan cross-examines National Bureau of Investigation Melvin Matibag on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on July 21, 2026. Maria Tan, ABS-CBN News MANILA — National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag gave his testimony on the eighth day of the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. Batangas 2nd District Rep. Gerville Luistro, lead House prosecutor, quizzed Matibag on the NBI's investigation into the alleged threats that Duterte made against Marcos Jr. and his relatives, including the possibility that she already had an arrangement with someone to do so. During her examination of Matibag, Luistro had a video of Duterte's brother Davao City Mayor Sebastian "Baste" Duterte speaking at a political rally in April where he seemed to call for Marcos Jr.'s head. Matibag said the video was relevant to the probe because it showed the vice president's 2024 statements were "a kinetic force" and that some who heard the alleged threats took her cue and made their own threats. Matibag told: ‘Avoid statements pertaining to members of impeachment court’ The NBI director said more than 600,000 people viewed the video of Mayor Duterte's statements, which he said shows the reach of the alleged threat. Matibag, like previous witnesses from the NBI, said the bureau took Duterte's statements seriously because of the potential threat to national security. The NBI director is the last prosecution witness on Duterte's alleged threats. LASCAÑAS AFFIDAVIT The prosecution also showed a 2011 video of Vice President Duterte punching a court sheriff when she was still Davao City mayor and featured an excerpt of alleged Davao Death Squad hitman Arturo Lascañas' affidavit on drug-related killings to repeated objections from defense counsel Mark Vinluan. Vinluan stressed the defense's objection to the Lascañas affidavit, which was submitted to the International Criminal Court but that Matibag had no personal knowledge on. "We cannot allow this witness to build his testimony based on this document," Vinluan also said, pointing out the affidavit is unsigned and was not notarized. Luistro said the video and the affidavit were material since the NBI considered these in its investigation. Matibag also referred to the affidavit as "open source intelligence" that the NBI used for leads. Escudero allowed the presentation of the affidavit but reminded senators that its contents were not necessarily true and that the impeachment court was not saying that they were. At a press briefing after the hearing, defense spokesperson Michael Poa declined to speculate on why prosecutors included the Lascañas statement but stressed its contents cannot be taken at face value. “Si Mr. Lascañas lang po ang puwedeng mag-identify ng sarili niyang affidavit and no one else,” he also said of the document, which was not notarized. Matibag later told the impeachment court that the NBI already has persons of interest — people who may be involved in an investigation but who are not suspects — but said he could not disclose who they are . "[U]nang-una pong mangyayari rito ay makokompromiso po ang ating imbestigasyon at mailalagay po sa alanganin yun pong ating mga tinatawag na informants o assets na nasa ground na nagbibigay sa atin ng human intel na tinatawag," he said. (First of all, it would compromsie the investigation and put our informants or assets on the ground giving us human [intelligence] at risk.) DEFENSE BRINGS UP MATIBAG'S WIFE, OPINION COLUMNS During cross-examination, Vinluan raised that Matibag is married to Laguna 1st District Rep. Ann Matibag, one of the House members who supported Duterte's impeachment. The NBI director said his wife's job "is totally detached" from his official duties. When confronted with opinion pieces critical of Duterte that he had written for The Daily Tribune as well as an art card showing the vice president has retained a high trust rating, Matibag said the NBI "cannot be swayed by public opinion [or our] personal opinion." He also told Vinluan that trust ratings in surveys are different from the public trust that the Articles of Impeachment allege Duterte broke. Matibag acknowledged that the Department of Justice, where the NBI filed its Inciting to Sedition and Grave Threats complaints against Duterte in February 2025, has yet to find basis for the allegation that the vice president actually contracted a killer. He said, though, that it is an open and continuing investigation. PIA CAYETANO SCOLDS PROSECUTION The defense asked to be allowed to continue cross-examination on Wednesday, giving senator-judges time to ask their own questions and to otherwise have the floor. Sen. Pia Cayetano, one of the few senators who are also lawyers, took Luistro to task for including the Lascañas affidavit that the defense had repeatedly objected to. She said the prosecution was "trying to prove something" by presenting the document and quoting from it even if Matibag had no personal knowledge on its contents and on how it was executed. She added that the quoted portion "cannot be unheard" even if Escudero had stressed that the affidavit's contents are hearsay. Cayetanos take impeachment issues to Facebook Live "Do your job and present the proper witness and the proper documentation to [prove your case]," she said in a rare raised voice in the trial day. — Jonathan de Santos, ABS-CBN News Trial resumes at 2 p.m. on Wednesday, July 22 MANILA — House prosecution legal spokesperson Atty. Benjamin Tolosa Jr. said on Tuesday that it is “normal” to interview witnesses before an impeachment trial. This was in response to the line of questioning by defense lawyer Attorney Mark Vinluan during the trial against Vice President Sara Duterte, which involved National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag. Vinluan asked Matibag, a witness, if he was briefed by Rep. Gerville Luistro when they met up before the trial. “And you are confirming in open court that you discussed or you were briefed in that meeting based on your testimony,” Vinluan said. This was met with a resounding expression of the word “Misleading!” from multiple individuals, seeming to come from the side where the prosecution sat. “Well, I'm a lawyer, and I know where you're going. There was no discussion or coaching,” Matibag replied. Tolosa stressed it is not irregular for a prosecutor to meet with a witness before they testify. “What he said is he had an opportunity to meet with the public prosecutor. But there is nothing unusual or irregular about that. Napakanormal ho ’yan sa lahat ng paglilitis – kahit sa normal na mga kaso. Normal ho ’yan. Bago ka mag-upo ng testigo, normal na kausapin mo, interview-hin mo ’yung witness para malaman mo ano bang masasabi niya dito sa paglilitis na ito,” Tolosa said. Observers from inside the session hall also caught wind of other events or reactions that may not have been seen on the livestream. Senate impeachment court presiding officer Senator Francis Escudero, Duterte’s lead counsel Atty. Sheila Sison, and House lead prosecutor and Batangas 2nd District Representative Gerville Luistro were spotted talking while the impeachment trial against Duterte was on recess. While the specific topic of discussion could not be heard from where observers stayed at the session hall, Escudero made reference to a discussion with counsel for the parties before the trial adjourned. Senator Juan Miguel Zubiri asked why the subpoenas for the appearance of former Land Bank branch managers Violeta Constantino and Nenita Camposano were to be withdrawn. “You are withdrawing the subpoena because you feel that we might not take them up tomorrow? [...] You mean, we cannot take it up tomorrow?” Zubiri asked. Escudero answered, “I would think so. That was pursuant to a discussion with both counsel for the parties earlier.” Only snippets of the conversation among Escudero, Sison, and Luistro could be heard, with the senator saying phrases such as, “I’m going to give you time to decide.” After adjournment, Tolosa, House prosecutor and Bicol Saro Representative Terry Ridon, and House prosecution panel spokesperson and Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Alonto Adiong held a press conference. However, they said they did not hear the conversation among the three. At many points throughout the trial, senator-judges temporarily exited the session hall. There were times when as few as 12 senators remained in their seats. At around 3:17 p.m., only Senators Escudero, Zubiri, Sherwin Gatchalian, Erwin Tulfo, Francis Pangilinan, Lito Lapid, Panfilo Lacson, JV Ejercito, Risa Hontiveros, Vicente Sotto III, Bam Aquino, and Pia Cayetano were still in the session hall. The number of senator-judges soon increased, but continued to fluctuate throughout the day. MANILA — National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag declined to identify the alleged "contracted assassin" and other persons of interest (POIs) linked to Vice President Sara Duterte during Tuesday's impeachment trial. Matibag was asked by the prosecution to identify the POIs but refused, citing the ongoing investigation. During a press conference after the hearing, Impeachment Court spokesperson Atty. Reginald Tongol was asked whether Matibag could disclose the identities of the POIs in an executive session. Tongol said such a scenario is possible, explaining that an executive session forms part of the Senate's legislative process and may be suppletorily applied under the Senate Impeachment Rules. “Base on my analysis of the rules po, under rule 6 of the senate impeachment rules, mababasa po ninyo doon na, suppletory applicable yung senate rules, pati po ng rules of court.” “Pag sinabi po nating suppletory applicable, pag hindi po sinasabi sa senate impeachment rules, yung mga ganung mga processo, pwede pang i-apply yung senate rules on the legislative process. Doon po may makikitang executive session at kung yun po yung balak gawin ng isang senator judge mag move po siya, then baka po viable possibility po yun na pwedeng mangyari.” Tongol noted, however, that none of the senator-judges has so far moved to hold an executive session for the possible disclosure of the identities of the persons of interest. He also reiterated that under Memorandum Circular No. 15, issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., Matibag is bound by confidentiality rules and is prohibited from disclosing the identities of the persons of interest because they are part of an ongoing investigation. Footage of a 2011 incident in which Vice President Sara Duterte, then mayor of Davao City, punched a sheriff during a demolition of shanties in the city. Screenshot from ABS-CBN News Channel on YouTube/File MANILA — A 2011 incident in which Vice President Sara Duterte, then mayor of Davao City, punched a sheriff was raised Tuesday during the Senate impeachment trial of the country's second-highest official. Footage of a television news report on the incident was played during the proceedings as National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag took the witness stand. Matibag cited the incident as one of the cases the NBI considered in establishing what it described as a "pattern of violence" while investigating allegations of grave threats made by Duterte against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The confrontation, captured on video, occurred during a demolition operation in Davao City in 2011. The sheriff involved, Abe Andres, is also listed among the prosecution's witnesses in the impeachment trial. Aside from the video, the NBI also obtained an affidavit from Arturo Lascañas, a former police officer and self-confessed member of the vigilante group Davao Death Squad. In the affidavit, Lascañas described Duterte as among the architects of Oplan Tokhang, the controversial anti-illegal drug campaign carried out during the administration of former President Rodrigo Duterte, the Vice President's father, Matibag narrated during his testimony. Matibag is serving as the prosecution's final witness on allegations of grave threats and inciting to sedition, which form part of the Articles of Impeachment against Duterte. The article of impeachment is mainly anchored on statements made by Duterte in which she claimed to have instructed someone to kill Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and Speaker Martin Romualdez should she be killed first. It also cites remarks in which Duterte said she imagined beheading the President. Rene Ann Lourdes "Ann" Matibag, endorsed House Resolution No. 989 that set forth the Articles of Impeachment against the vice president. He said that he was testifying at the impeachment court because he had been summoned and by the invitation of the House impeachment panel. “However, the job of my wife as a legislator is totally detached from me being the director of the National Bureau of Investigation,” he said. The court did not issue a subpoena for Matibag, who later clarified that he is appearing “as a witness as called upon by this honorable court.” ‘PREMATURE, TRIAL BY PUBLICITY’ Vinluan asked whether Matibag’s testimony that the NBI has identified “persons of interest” in its probe is “premature,” after confirming that it is part of the standard operating procedure (SOP) to give Duterte a chance to be confronted with the findings. “Considering that you’re still pursuing those leads, don’t you think that your testimony today is premature?” Vinluan said. Matibag responded: “Hindi po. Sapagkat malinaw naman po sa statement ng ating bise presidente na meron siyang kinausap para patayin si Bongbong Marcos, si Liza Marcos Araneta, si Martin Romualdez." (No, because the vice president's statement that she had talked to someone to kill Bongbong Marcos, Liza Marcos Araneta and Martin Romualdez was clear.) He said Duterte's statement, made in a streamed online conference, was a "clear confession" by someone who had plans to have people killed.. Matibag: Sara Duterte remarks vs Marcos a threat to national security Vinluan also asked whether the agency is attempting trial by publicity. Matibag rejected this, citing NBI’s refusal to publicize the details of its investigation. Asked whether his testimony that the NBI has leads would prejudice the ongoing investigation, Matibag said he did not name the persons of interest precisely to avoid compromising an ongoing probe. LEAKED VIDEO Vinluan also raised a leaked video of an argument between Matibag and his friend, Mel Sabio, asking whether it demonstrated "an emotional outburst" on Matibag's part. In response, Matibag acknowledged that his statements in the video were made out of "galit at (anger and) disappointment," but said he has since regretted his remarks. Although the specific statements were not discussed during the hearing, reports said the recording captured Matibag threatening to kill Sabio. Vinluan also presented a Daily Tribune graphic showing the results of a recent Social Weather Stations survey , in which Duterte received a 57-percent public trust rating. Citing opinion pieces Matibag wrote for the same publication, including one in which he said public trust in the Vice President was crumbling, Vinluan asked whether he believed Duterte had betrayed public trust despite her high survey ratings. Matibag said surveys are merely "snapshots", saying also that the NBI "cannot be swayed by public opinion [or our] personal opinion." Matibag said public trust ratings in surveys are different from betrayal of public trust — an allegation in the Articles of Impeachment. "Kapag ating pinagbasehan ang popularidad, ibig sabihin ba nito, ang isang pinakakilala at popular na tao ay puwede nang gumawa ng krimen at hindi natin papapanagutin?" he said. (If our basis is popularity, does it mean that a well-known and popular person can commit a crime and not be held accountable?) 'Pattern of violence'? Duterte's sheriff-punching incident raised in impeachment trial ‘HEARSAY’ The defense also dismissed Matibag’s knowledge of the agency’s investigation into Duterte’s “grave threats” before his appointment as director February this year as “hearsay.” Matibag said he learned about the proceedings and findings through investigation reports and “upon the discussion of the investigating officers.” The counsel then cited the rules on evidence stating that “a witness can testify only to those facts which he or she knows of his or her personal knowledge that is, which are derived from his or her own perception.” Vinluan then said that a testimony, “if not based on personal knowledge, then that is hearsay.” WATCH

output.title: NBI probes Taguig flood projects; DOJ says no order issued
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) is investigating flood control projects in Taguig City, even as the Department of Justice (DOJ) clarified Monday that it did not order the probe.
output.text:
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) on Monday said it started its investigation into flood control projects in Taguig City, even as the Department of Justice (DOJ) clarified Monday that it did not order the probe.

NBI Director Melvin Matibag said the bureau was already looking into 11 flood control projects implemented in 2022 that were allegedly linked to some of the country's top 15 contractors.

“In fact, we are already investigating, kasi nung 2022 merong 11 proyekto diyan na somehow related doon sa mga pinangalanan na Top 15 contractors,” Matibag told reporters.

(In fact, we are already investigating because, in 2022, there were 11 projects there that were somehow linked to those named among the top 15 contractors.)

“Baka sabihin ninyo timing na naman. Anyway, public na naman ‘yan dahil sinasabi ni Senator Lacson, so I think we should mention it,” he added.

(You might say this is about timing again. Anyway, this is already public knowledge because Senator Lacson mentioned it, so I think we should mention it.)

Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida, however, stressed that the DOJ did not direct the NBI to conduct the investigation, saying the bureau was acting under its own mandate.

“We will respect the independence of the NBI relative to their mandate to pursue investigations. First thing, hindi ito pinag-utos ng DOJ. This is pursuant to the mandate of the NBI to pursue all this,” Vida said.

(We will respect the independence of the NBI in carrying out its mandate to pursue investigations. First, the DOJ did not order this. This is pursuant to the NBI's mandate to pursue these matters.)

Vida said that should the case reach the DOJ, the department would act based on the evidence presented.

“Kung sakaling makarating sa DOJ ‘yan, it will be based on what are the pieces of evidence presented. Rule of law pa rin tayo,” he said.

(If that reaches the DOJ, our action will be based on the evidence presented. We still abide by the rule of law.)

On Sunday, Senate Blue Ribbon Committee chairperson Senator Erwin Tulfo told fellow Senator Alan Peter Cayetano to be ready for an investigation into Taguig's flood control projects.

Cayetano's brother, former Taguig Mayor and current PTV general manager Lino Cayetano, who served as city mayor from 2019 to 2022, had sought an investigation into P6 billion worth of flood control projects implemented in Taguig from 2022 to 2025.

Vida also said ongoing investigations by other agencies should not be viewed as a distraction for senator-judges.

“Hindi dapat dahil ‘yung paghahabol natin ng accountability, hindi naman tumitigil ‘yun. Pare-parehong may ginagampanan, at ginagalang natin ang mga Senator-Judges,” Vida said.

(It should not be, because our pursuit of accountability does not stop. We all have our respective roles to play, and we respect the senator-judges.)

“And sa akin, kung wala namang dapat ipangamba about sa rule of law, wala dapat ipangamba ang mga senator-judges,” he added.

(And for me, if there is nothing to fear from the rule of law, then the senator-judges have nothing to fear.)

According to Vida, the NBI investigation is not yet barred by prescription, meaning authorities may still legally investigate and prosecute any alleged offenses arising from the projects. — MCG GMA News

output.title: Matibag to shed light on probe into VP Sara Duterte's 'kill' threat — spox
output.description: National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is expected to shed light on the agency’s probe into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged death threat against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., when he testifies before the impeachment court on Tuesday, the prosecution panel said Sunday.
output.text:
National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Director Melvin Matibag is expected to shed light on the agency’s probe into Vice President Sara Duterte’s alleged death threat against President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr., when he testifies before the impeachment court on Tuesday, the prosecution panel said Sunday.

In an interview on Super Radyo dzBB on Sunday, Atty. Benjamin Tolosa said Matibag is expected to provide key details that the first two witnesses could not cover due to the limited scope of their work.

“Lagi niya hong sinasabi [na] ang makakasagot diyan ay ‘yung intelligence service na, so diyan ho papasok si NBI Director Melvin Matibag,” Tolosa said, referring to the testimony of NBI Cybercrime Division chief Jeremy Lotoc.

(He kept saying that the intelligence service would be able to answer that, so that is where NBI Director Melvin Matibag comes in.)

“Siya ho ang makakapagbigay-linaw tungkol sa kung ano ang masusing imbestigasyon na ginawa ng NBI patungkol dito sa mamamatay-tao na kinausap ng bise presidente,” he added.

(He can shed light on the NBI’s thorough investigation into the alleged assassin whom the Vice President said she had spoken to.)

Tolosa also argued that the article of impeachment accusing Duterte of making grave threats against the President, First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then-House Speaker Martin Romualdez could be supported by her own statements and her refusal to retract the alleged threat.

“Meron ba talagang kinausap na mamamatay-tao?... Napakaliwanag na po ng sagot diyan, meron. Ano ho ang pruweba natin? ‘Yung tinatawag na admission against interest ng bise presidente, sa kanya na po nanggaling 'yan,” Tolosa said.

(Did she really talk to an assassin? The answer to that is already very clear: yes. What is our proof? What we call the Vice President’s admission against interest—it came from her herself.)

Tolosa said an admission against interest is among the strongest forms of evidence under the Rules of Court because it comes directly from the person against whom it is being used.

“Lalo na dito, binigyan siya ng pagkakataon, three days after, para bawiin ito… pero hindi ho niya binawi yon. In fact, lalo pa niya hong diniin na talagang meron pero tinry ho lang niyang i-justify ‘yan by saying wala namang criminal act na revenge from the grave,” he said.

(Especially in this case, she was given an opportunity three days later to retract it, but she did not. In fact, she doubled down on it and merely tried to justify it by saying that there is no criminal act in seeking revenge from beyond the grave.)

Asked about the possibility that some senator-judges could question Matibag over the NBI’s separate investigation into alleged anomalies surrounding the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, Tolosa expressed confidence that the presiding officer would ensure that the proceedings remain focused on the impeachment case.

“At the end of the day, umaasa pa rin kami na tatalima pa rin ang mga senator-judges doon ho sa requirements under their own rules, not to unduly discriminate against anyone,” Tolosa said.

(At the end of the day, we still hope that the senator-judges will adhere to the requirements under their own rules and not unduly discriminate against anyone.)

On July 15, the NBI announced plans to create a task force to investigate alleged anomalies in the bidding and funding of projects related to the Philippines’ hosting of the 2019 SEA Games.

Senator Alan Peter Cayetano served as chairperson of the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), which organized the country’s hosting of the regional sporting event.

The NBI investigation has drawn scrutiny from Cayetano and Senators Pia Cayetano and Robin Padilla, who questioned its timing amid the ongoing impeachment trial of Vice President Duterte.— MCG GMA News

output.title: NBI to file raps over P55 million SEAG cauldron
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation is set to file cases in the coming days over alleged irregularities related to the “golden cauldron” installed for the 2019 Southeast Asian (SEA) Games, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said. Speaking at a forum in Quezon City over the weekend, Matibag said the investigation had yielded documents and testimonies that could support criminal charges. “Within the next few days, perhaps within a week, we will be filing cases,” Matibag said. The investigation is part of the NBI’s broader probe into the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC), which Matibag said involves multiple cases and a large volume of documents and testimonies. “We divided this into pieces so we can file cases. There will be different cases coming out. The cauldron is another case. That might be the first one,” he said. Matibag said the NBI had obtained documents concerning the cauldron, which reportedly cost P55 million, although the actual cost was allegedly only about P5 million. He said several leaders of sports associations were also being investigated, with some already appearing before the NBI after receiving subpoenas. Matibag said the NBI was also examining the activities of people associated with Sen. Alan Peter Cayetano, who was the head of PHISGOC in 2019. He identified sports executive Ramon Suzara as among those being looked into, noting that some PHISGOC members had been Cayetano’s colleagues, staff members or associates. “We are still developing and checking what ventures they are involved in,” Matibag said. The NBI is also looking into why PHISGOC continued to sponsor international events despite being created specifically to organize the 2019 SEA Games. “It was supposed to end its existence after the SEA Games. But we found out that until now, they are still sponsoring international events. We are looking into that,” Matibag said. Matibag stressed that the PHISGOC investigation remains ongoing and that the NBI is pursuing separate cases based on the evidence it has gathered. output.title: NBI chief Matibag did NOT step down
output.description: A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post. Not true.
output.text: Melvin Matibag stepped down from his post as director of the National Bureau of Investigation. As of May 21, Melvin Matibag continues to serve as NBI director. Reports that NBI agents who attempted to serve an ICC arrest warrant for Sen. Bato Dela Rosa “betrayed” him are false. A claim is circulating on social media that National Bureau of Investigation Director Melvin Matibag has left his post following the May 11 mayhem at the Senate involving an attempt to arrest Sen. Bato Dela Rosa. Not true. The NBI chief did not step down. The false claim originated from a YouTube channel that published a video on May 12 with a thumbnail that bore the text: “ MATIBAG BUMITAW NA. SENADO TINAPOS SI MATIBAG SA NBI? 9-NBI AGENT NILAGLAG SI MATIBAG (MATIBAG HAD STEPPED DOWN. SENATE ENDED MATIBAG AT NBI? 9 NBI AGENTS BETRAYED MATIBAG)” It surfaced the day after Dela Rosa appeared at the Senate for the first time since November 2025, when news came out that the International Criminal Court had issued a warrant for his arrest in connection with the crimes against humanity case in which the senator is named as a co-conspirator. NBI agents attempted to serve the arrest warrant, which prompted Dela Rosa to run, leading to a chase on a staircase from the parking area to the session hall, where the senator eventually obtained protective custody from Senate President Alan Peter Cayetano. Matibag continues to hold his position at the NBI. On May 21, he went to Legazpi City to lead the inauguration of the NBI Academy in the Bicol Region. The nine NBI personnel involved in chasing Dela Rosa were cited in contempt at the Senate and have since been turned over to the NBI as the bureau conducts its own investigation into the matter. There have been no reports from authorities or from the media that they “betrayed” Matibag in any way. The false claim gained attention anew after three other YouTube channels published their versions of the graphic from May 15 to 16 with some visual enhancements, such as adjusting saturation levels, blurring/unblurring some faces, and switching the placement of the text and pictures. Several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts then pushed out these graphics in the same time period, a few days after gunshots rang out within the Senate premises on the evening of May 13. Dela Rosa was then still under protective custody of the Senate. The publishers on FB notably used hashtags like #ddssolidsupporters #protectvpsarah (sic) and #pilipinasduterteparin. Four separate YouTube channels have used the false thumbnail for their videos, namely PINAS NEWS INSIDER (the original publisher), PINAS NEWS INSIGHT , KOMENTARYO PH, and KAPANIG NG MASA . Their clips have collectively gotten over 300,000 views, 16,000 likes, and 2,100 comments. VERA Files Fact Check has also flagged nine posts on FB that reposted the graphic. output.title: Obstruction raps eyed over Bato’s escape
output.description: The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend.
output.text: MANILA, Philippines — The National Bureau of Investigation and the Office of the Ombudsman are investigating a possible obstruction of justice complaint over the escape of Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa from the Senate, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said over the weekend. Matibag said NBI agents involved in the incident had submitted their affidavits to the ombudsman as part of the investigation.? “One of the cases now being studied by the ombudsman, together with the NBI and the Department of Justice, is obstruction of justice concerning the incident at the Senate of the Philippines,” Matibag told GMA News on Saturday. He said the affidavits had earlier been submitted during the DOJ investigation and could be used as testimonial evidence if charges are filed. “If there are cases to be filed in whichever court, whether the Sandiganbayan or another court, these affidavits will be used as testimonial evidence, and our agents will cooperate in the proceedings,” Matibag said. He said the NBI agents’ testimonies would be supported by independent witnesses and physical evidence, including media accounts and closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage. “The testimony of the NBI will matter a lot. There are also independent personalities who will testify, including members of the media. Aside from that, we have object evidence, CCTV footage and videos captured by the media,” he said. The probe stemmed from the May 13 shooting incident at the Senate, where 12 to 15 gunshots were heard during a standoff between Senate security personnel and NBI agents searching for Dela Rosa. Dela Rosa had been staying inside the Senate amid an impending arrest over an International Criminal Court warrant related to the previous administration’s drug war. Dela Rosa left the Senate with Sen. Robinhood Padilla early on May 14. A DOJ special prosecutor panel later concluded that the Senate had not been under attack and that the actions of then-acting Senate sergeant-at-arms Mao Aplasca were not justified. Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla dismissed Aplasca on June 25 for grave misconduct and gross neglect of duty over the shooting incident.? The ombudsman is expected to determine whether sufficient evidence exists to bring charges before the courts. output.title: FACT CHECK: Bato dela Rosa did NOT surrender to NBI
output.description: Several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are claiming that Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa, who is the subject of an International Criminal Court warrant, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. This is false.
output.text: Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. No verified reports support claims that Dela Rosa surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said the lawmaker has yet to be apprehended, noting that a manhunt to locate dela Rosa is ongoing. Amid rumors of a supposed arrest, several pro-Duterte Facebook accounts are capitalizing on posts claiming that Sen. Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is the subject of a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, has surrendered to the National Bureau of Investigation. The posts are untrue and designed to attract clicks for monetization. VERA Files traced the earliest copy of the claim to an Aug. 3 post by an FB page advocating for the 2028 presidential bid of Vice President Sara Duterte. It carried a photo set of the fugitive lawmaker interacting with men in uniform. The post also bore the caption, “Senator bato delarosà sumukó na [shocked emoji] Sa mga NBÎ at nag salita at humingi… (Senator Bato dela Rosa has surrendered to the NBI, spoke out, and pleaded…),” but ended with the phrase “see more,” creating the impression that additional details would follow. A tactic employed by some disinformation peddlers previously flagged by VERA Files, the teaser seemed intended to entice users to click the photo set, which contained an embedded link that redirects them to a product page on a popular e-commerce platform. No verified reports substantiate online claims that dela Rosa surrendered to the NBI. In fact, the agency’s Director Melvin Matibag said that the senator wanted by the ICC has yet to be apprehended, adding that their manhunt operation to locate dela Rosa is still ongoing. The photos used in the spurious posts appeared to be screenshots from a video originally posted by a certain Alvin Go on May 13, after the shooting incident in the Senate. In the clip , dela Rosa was seen shaking hands with a police officer, not an NBI agent or official. Notably, the fraudulent posts began circulating a day before the FB post of Jimmy Bondoc, one of dela Rosa’s counsels, saying: “Bad news is coming. Pray hard that it is not true, for the good of the nation.” The cryptic message, which can no longer be found on Bondoc’s official page, supposedly fueled speculations of dela Rosa’s arrest, according to some news reports . Dela Rosa has remained at large since May 14 following a gun-firing incident in the Senate as authorities earlier attempted to serve him the ICC warrant. The former police chief and enforcer of ex-president Rodrigo Duterte’s brutal anti-drug campaign is wanted by the international tribunal for the crime against humanity of murder in relation to the killing of at least 32 people between July 2016 and April 2018. From Aug. 3 to 5, VERA Files identified at least 34 FB posts spreading the untrue claim. Their closely spaced publication times—from as little as a minute to several hours apart—raise the possibility of coordinated activity. All posts used the photo set as a thumbnail to disguise affiliate links to several products on Lazada and Shopee, including food, cosmetics, phone cases, portable fans, and water tumblers. The links earn commissions for the accounts whenever netizens click and make purchases. As of writing, the clickbait posts by Inday sa 2028 (created on Oct. 23, 2022 as Ver0níca Kittty D. ), Kitty Duterte fanpage (July 11, 2023) and DU30 KITTY VEE (created on May 27, 2020 as Ｎａｔｈａｎ 願今。 ), among others, collectively garnered over 1,000 reactions. Another notable observation is a mismatch between the little to no interactions on posts from some of the documented FB pages and their thousands of followers.
